hpi: The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of alcohol use disorder who presents with abdominal pain. He has been experiencing this pain for the past week. The pain is described as sharp and located in the epigastric region. He reports nausea and vomiting. On examination, he appears in mild distress. Laboratory tests reveal elevated liver enzymes and a CT scan shows thickening of the gastric wall. The patient is diagnosed with acute gastritis likely secondary to alcohol use. Management includes supportive care, avoidance of NSAIDs, and counseling on alcohol cessation.
